skill.name: design-an-interface
skill.description: Generate multiple radically different interface designs for a module using parallel sub-agents. Use when user wants to design an API, explore interface options, compare module shapes, or mentions "design it twice".
skill.summary: Explore several software interface designs, compare trade-offs, and choose a clearer module shape.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown code fence in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only and guides interface design exploration; no executable commands, data access, or prompt injection attempts were found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 28 begins a Markdown fenced block that contains a sub-agent prompt template, not Ruby or shell execution. No executable code or command invocation is present in the file.

content.value_statement: Many teams choose the first API shape they imagine, which can create shallow modules and awkward callers. This skill uses Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to generate distinct interface options and compare trade-offs.
actual_capabilities: Gathers module requirements before proposing interface shapes.
Prompts multiple sub-agents to create different design directions.
Compares interface simplicity, depth, flexibility, and misuse risks.
Presents usage examples for each proposed design.
Helps synthesize a final interface from stronger design ideas.
limitations: It does not implement the selected interface.
It depends on clear requirements from the user.
It does not run benchmarks or validate performance claims.
It focuses on module APIs, not visual product interfaces.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Module API
use_cases.description: Explore several caller-facing shapes before committing to a public interface.

use_cases.title: Review Library Design Options
use_cases.description: Compare compact, flexible, and common-case designs for a shared package.

use_cases.title: Improve Technical Design Documents
use_cases.description: Add alternative interface proposals and trade-off analysis to architecture notes.

prompt_templates.title: Start Interface Exploration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple module design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an interface for a module that manages user notification preferences. Ask for missing requirements first.

prompt_templates.title: Compare API Shapes
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three different interfaces for a feature flag service. Compare simplicity, flexibility, depth, and misuse risks in prose.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with a current API that feels awkward.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to redesign our current payment adapter interface. Keep compatibility concerns visible and propose migration-friendly alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Final Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request after several candidate designs exist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed interfaces, identify the strongest ideas, and synthesize one final module interface with clear trade-offs.

output_examples.input: Design an interface for a document export module.
output_examples.output: Three interface directions: a minimal export command, a configurable export service, and a workflow-based design. Each includes caller usage and trade-offs.

output_examples.input: Compare designs for a permission checking API.
output_examples.output: A prose comparison covering method count, ease of correct use, hidden complexity, future extension, and misuse risks.

output_examples.input: Synthesize the best interface from these options.
output_examples.output: A recommended direction that combines the simplest caller API with explicit extension points and a short migration note.

best_practices: Provide the main callers, operations, and constraints before asking for designs.
Ask for designs that optimize for different goals.
Compare trade-offs before choosing a final interface.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when implementation code is the immediate deliverable.
Accepting similar designs without forcing meaningful contrast.
Choosing the largest interface because it supports every possible future case.

faq.question: Does this skill write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on interface shape, caller experience, and trade-off analysis.

faq.question: Can it help with TypeScript APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose type and method shapes when you provide module requirements.

faq.question: Why does it use multiple sub-agents?
faq.answer: It uses separate design directions to avoid settling on the first idea too early.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Share the current interface and constraints, then ask for alternative designs.

faq.question: Does it evaluate implementation effort?
faq.answer: No. The skill prioritizes interface clarity, depth, flexibility, and correct use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
